learning_outcomes.text: Participants of the course Industrial Production understand how industrial production companies operate.
They explain the product creation process and describe the roles played by the functions of product planning, development/design, work planning and control, sales, purchasing, production/assembly.
They explain the associated information flows as well as organisational and management concepts.

On the basis of example scenarios, students outline structures and processes of a producing company and apply concepts for the organisation, planning and control of product development and production.

The students understand the functioning of producing industrial companies and are able to classify the typical engineering tasks in an industrial company within the overall context of product creation.

syllabus_topics: Systems Engineering: System thinking; Process models; System design
Introduction to project management: What is a project?; Project types and systematics of project management
People in the project: The role of the project leader; Project success and team roles; Myers-Briggs Type Indicator; Stakeholder analysis
Project definition: Definition of project goals; Project and process organization; Development systematics; Information organization and project management manual
Project planning: Structural planning (product, project, account structure); Network planning technique; Schedule and cost planning; Risk management
Project control: Actual/target comparison of deadlines and costs; Reports; Management information system; Project documentation
Project completion: Project acceptance; Crisis management; Experience consolidation
assessment_rules: The allocation of credit points takes place when the module examination has been passed. In the exam, students should explain basic concepts of industrial production and project management and transfer what they have learned to similar problems.
